newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks rebound, market recovery in sight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks rebound, market recovery in sight.

text.p: Croatian stocks rebounded on Friday, ending the mixed week on a positive note which market participants saw as a first sign of a long-awaited recovery.
They said bargain hunters were finally drawn by very low levels most active issues had dropped to, and stronger buying interest in turn spurred a slight price rise.
"Some prices may well pick up next week, though not by much," said one trader at a large bank with foreign clients, thought to be the main driving force of the young market.
Their absence, ahead of local elections set for April 13, has been blamed for causing the recent slump after an unexpected rally very early in the year.
Addition of two new issues -- Varazdinska Banka ordinary and preferred stocks -- to the top bourse bracket on April 8 is hoped to attract back at least some investors.
"People are still nervous of buying," the trader said, adding that most buyers were likely to hold their orders till after the election.
But one analyst said next week's profit announcement of the market heavyweight Zagrebacka Banka might bring forward a definite reversal of the downward trend, otherwise forecast for later this month.
Zagrebacka's ordinary stock regained another five kuna to close at 1,800 on volume of 665 shares. Preferred E-series also inched up four kuna to 965 with 112 units changing hands.
Six out of 12 active stocks rose and five were flat on Friday in moderate trade on turnover of 2.7 million kuna. Volume shrank slightly to 4,104 units.
Blue chip Pliva was the day's only loser, dipping 10 kuna to 440 on a volume of 326 shares after staying off the market on Thursday.

Although most traders say this is a very good price for Pliva, investors seem to be waiting to see if rumours about its 1996 net not being much changed from a year earlier are true. It is due to release last year's figures later this month.
Gainers were led by hotelier Istraturist, which rose 10 kuna to 180, or 5.88 percent from a fortnight ago. But its prospects were said to be dim until nearer the tourist season.
Most active issue was food concern Podravka with 1,395 shares traded, closing three kuna higher at 298.
Varazdinska Banka added 25 kuna to 42,025, but sold only one ordinary share.

Among the stocks that remained steady were privatisation candidate Koncar at 1,300 kuna and chocolate maker Kras at 420. Hoteliers Laguna, Suncani Hvar and Zlatni Rat also closed flat at 1,450, 60 and 150 kuna respectively.
